title: Intel Stock Faces 87 Million-Share Risk After SoftBank Deal
detail:
Intel Stock Faces 87 Million-Share Risk After SoftBank Deal
Phil Haunhorst
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 1:34 PM MST 3 min read
9984.T
INTC
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Intel stock crash after weak Q4 forecast despite 78% AI revenue growth. Photo by BeInCrypto

Intel investors have another risk to consider after SoftBank revealed losses tied to its 87 million shares in the chipmaker.

The Japanese investment giant has already raised $7.4 billion against its entire stake, raising questions about whether those shares could eventually return to the market.

According to SoftBank's November 10 disclosure, the company entered prepaid forward contracts in August. These arrangements allow investors to receive cash upfront in exchange for settling the contracts later, potentially by delivering shares.

The contracts cover roughly 1.6% of Intel's outstanding shares.

However, SoftBank has not disclosed a timetable for selling or delivering those shares. The full 87 million should therefore not be treated as confirmed future selling pressure.

Why Does This Matter for Intel Stock?

SoftBank originally paid $2 billion for its Intel stake in 2025. By September 30, its value had surged to $10.5 billion.

But Intel's subsequent decline changed the picture.

The shares fell from $120.23 in September to $58.13 on November 10, cutting the stake's market value to approximately $5.1 billion.

That is now below the $7.4 billion SoftBank received through its financing deal, although it does not automatically trigger a forced sale.

SoftBank also reported approximately $2 billion in derivative losses and $1.7 billion in Intel valuation losses during the September quarter.

SoftBank's Intel Shareholding and Fair Value. Source: SoftBank Group

Meanwhile, Intel has struggled through the broader technology sell-off. Shares plunged approximately 30% on October 30 after the company forecast weaker fourth-quarter revenue and warned about continued PC demand weakness.

Intel recovered around 8% during Wednesday's trading as stronger AI infrastructure sentiment lifted semiconductor stocks.

Does Wall Street Still Expect an Intel Stock Recovery?

Despite the sell-off, Wall Street remains cautiously optimistic about Intel's recovery.

According to S&P Global analyst estimates, 49 analysts have an average 12-month price target of $91.12, with a consensus Hold rating.

However, several banks recently lowered their expectations. Citi reduced its target from $130 to $100, while JPMorgan cut its forecast to $80.

Intel's own outlook also remains uncertain.

Intel Stock Crashed 40% In a Month. Source: Google Finance

CFO David Zinsner warned that the company expects the PC slowdown to continue "at least through the first half of next year."

SoftBank's financing arrangement does not directly change Intel's long-term business prospects. Investors should watch for further disclosures about the contracts, particularly settlement dates and potential share deliveries.

SoftBank's investor briefing shows the fair value of its Intel stake rose to 1,645.1 billion, or $10.5 billion, at September 30 from 613.5 billion, or $3.8 billion, at March 31. That produced a 1,062.8 billion Intel valuation gain for the six months. That is an inference, as SoftBank did not detail the terms. title: Amkor's Communications Business Weakens: Can a Recovery Take Hold?
detail:
Amkor's Communications Business Weakens: Can a Recovery Take Hold?
Subhasish Mukherjee
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:19 AM MST 3 min read
AMKR
INTC
GFS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Amkor Technology AMKR is grappling with a sharp contraction in its Communications business, as smartphone-related production disruptions and material constraints weigh on sales. Communications revenues declined 28% year over year and 8% sequentially in third-quarter 2026. The end market accounted for 37% of total revenues, down from 51% a year earlier, limiting consolidated revenue growth to just 0.2%.

The weakness primarily reflects the strategic migration of system-in-package (SiP) programs from Korea to Vietnam and associated preproduction activities. Memory supply constraints, higher component costs and changes in smartphone build patterns have added pressure. Management expects these headwinds to persist into the fourth quarter, with Communications revenues projected to decline a high-single-digit percentage sequentially. Both iOS- and Android-related business is expected to weaken, while lower-tier Android devices face greater difficulty absorbing higher memory prices.

Nevertheless, the transfer could improve Amkor's longer-term operating model. Management sees a meaningful SiP pipeline and expects business to rebound as Vietnamese production scales. The move also frees Korean cleanroom capacity for higher-value advanced packaging. Meanwhile, Computing and Automotive and Industrial revenues each rose 37% year over year in the third quarter, cushioning the Communications decline and supporting gross-margin expansion to 18.3% from 14.3% a year earlier.

A Communications recovery therefore appears possible, but not imminent. Its pace depends on completing the SiP transition, easing supply constraints and stronger smartphone demand; for now, growth elsewhere offers the clearer offset.

AMKR Faces Stiff Competition in Advanced Chip Packaging

GlobalFoundries GFS poses competition to Amkor through advanced packaging solutions for mobile connectivity chips. GlobalFoundries has qualified its SLATE wafer-bonding technology for compact 5G radio-frequency components, potentially improving semiconductor integration and efficiency. Although primarily a foundry rather than a traditional outsourced assembly-and-test provider, GlobalFoundries offers integrated manufacturing and packaging capabilities that could intensify competition for selected communications-related semiconductor programs.

Intel INTC competes with Amkor through advanced packaging technologies, including Foveros 3D stacking and EMIB interconnect solutions. Intel is strengthening its position in heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based architectures, targeting AI and high-performance computing applications. Intel's extensive manufacturing infrastructure and advanced packaging expertise could intensify competition for high-value semiconductor projects, although Amkor maintains a stronger focus on outsourced packaging and smartphone-related SiP services.

Key Takeaways

AMD jumped 4% after CoreWeave raised its 2026 revenue forecast.

CoreWeave's growing backlog supports AMD's guidance for server revenue to double next year.

Intel and Arm sell into the same boom, and UBS has Arm taking server CPU share from Intel.

AMD trades near its average forward P/E, with analysts expecting its earnings to more than double in 2027.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) shares are up 4% today after CoreWeave beat estimates and raised its 2026 outlook.

Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) is rising on the same news, and Arm Holdings (ARM:NASDAQ) keeps winning server CPU share.

CoreWeave's backlog backs AMD's big guide

CoreWeave's third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion. Its backlog climbed to $132.5 billion from about $104 billion in June, and its 2026 forecast now beats the $12.9 billion analysts expected. Most of that money goes to Nvidia's chips. But demand this strong outruns what any one supplier can ship, and that's AMD's opening.

On CNBC's Closing Bell Tuesday, Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon summed up AMD's guide: "AMD is effectively guiding for their server revenues next year to double and their GPU revenues to almost triple."

Analysts expect AMD's revenue to nearly double in 2027, to $95.9 billion:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

CoreWeave's quarter gives analysts no reason to cut those numbers.

Intel is short on chips, and Arm is filling the gap

Intel is up 6% too. Its Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion in the third quarter, but it can't make enough chips.

UBS's Timothy Arcuri said Wednesday that third-quarter server CPU shipments rose 31% from a year earlier. Arm's unit share rose about 2.5 points to 20.1% and Intel's fell to 51.5%, while AMD's stayed roughly flat at 28.4%. So for now, AMD's server growth is coming from a fast-growing market.

TIKR tracks 53 analysts on AMD. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AMD, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AMD's Analyst Ratings

AMD trades near its usual multiple

AMD's forward P/E was 34x at the last close. That's around its five-year average of 35x and half its June peak of 67x:

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's a bit higher. Investors are paying a normal multiple because analysts expect normalized EPS to more than double, from $8.08 this year to $17.69 in 2027.

CoreWeave's quarter makes those numbers easier to believe, and AMD doesn't need a bigger multiple to work from here. The risk is interest rates. CoreWeave's $846 million of interest expense last quarter was four times its $207 million of operating income. AMD's fourth-quarter report in early February is the next test.
